newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- The record rise of the dollar versus the drachma raises concerns over the impact on consumer price inflation. The issue will be discussed today between finance and national economy minister Yiannos Papandoniou and the deputy development minister Michael Hrysohoides. A decision to slash taxation on petrol is on the cards.

-- The last regulations on cross-border capital flows and foreign currency holdings by Greek residents remaining in place may be lifted as early as today by the Bank of Greece. The plan would have gone ahead in May 1997 but was aborted following a brief episode of weakness of the drachma.

-- A top government meeting to be held today will look into cuts in third-party taxation in an effort to drive consumer price inflation lower. Indirect taxation is already believed to be at critically low levels in respect of fiscal policy targets for the coming two years.

-- The deputy national economy minister Christos Pahtas is expected to round up by Thursday his meetings with fellow ministers before submitting the second set of proposals for co-funding of projects and business intiiatives by the European Union's Community Support Framework.
-- Preliminary data from the processing of income tax statements shows that fiscal revenues from pensioners and employees have risen substantially, in contrast to self-employed professionals.

-- Within this week the Bank of Greece will abolish all regulations on foreign currency holdings by Greek residents but removal of limitations to the movement of short-term funds in and out of Greece will have to wait for a while.
-- The rise of the dollar in international markets poses problems for Greece in so far as fuel prices are playing up and the cost of servicing Greece's external debt has risen.
-- Upbeat half-year profitability of banks has brought a euphoric mood to investors in the Greek stock exchange.
-- Unjustifiably steep price increases in food and imported apparel will be looked into by the development ministry's Monopolies Commission.
-- Today's auction of seven-year floating rate notes from which the government seeks to raise 125 billion drachmas is seen critical for the course of interest rates.
-- More banks announce record profit growth. This time it was NIBID, Xiosbank and ErgoBank. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
